descriptions.lru-cache-11.3.6/dist/esm/index.js#isPos: This function takes any value and returns true only if it is a finite, positive, whole number of numeric type; otherwise it returns false.
descriptions.lru-cache-11.3.6/dist/esm/index.js#getUi: Given a maximum value, it returns the smallest unsigned integer typed-array constructor able to hold it, a fallback array type for larger safe integers, or nothing for invalid inputs.
descriptions.lru-cache-11.3.6/dist/esm/index.js#ZeroA: This creates a specialized array of a given length, taking a size and producing a new array with every element initialized to zero.
descriptions.lru-cache-11.3.6/dist/esm/index.js#shoul: It takes a warning identifier and returns true if that identifier isn't yet in an existing collection of already-issued warnings, meaning a warning should still be shown.
descriptions.lru-cache-11.3.6/dist/esm/index.js#Stack: This is a fixed-capacity integer stack that, given a maximum size, is backed by the smallest fitting unsigned typed array; if no such array fits, a plain empty array is returned instead.
descriptions.lru-cache-11.3.6/dist/esm/index.js##init: This method takes no arguments and returns nothing; it sets up the cache's per-entry expiration machinery for setting lifetimes, refreshing ages, optional automatic purge timers, remaining-time lookup, and staleness checks.
descriptions.lru-cache-11.3.6/dist/esm/index.js#getNo: It takes no arguments and returns the current high-resolution timestamp, caching it briefly and scheduling a non-blocking timer to clear that cache after a configured resolution interval.
descriptions.lru-cache-11.3.6/dist/esm/index.js#pop@7: This method takes no arguments, shrinks the stored count by one, and returns the last element of the internal array without actually clearing that slot.
descriptions.lru-cache-11.3.6/dist/esm/index.js#push@: This method takes a single value, places it at the next open position at the end of the internal storage, increments the stored count, returns nothing, and does no reordering.
descriptions.lru-cache-11.3.6/dist/esm/index.js##init: Taking no arguments and returning nothing, it sets up a cache's size tracking: a per-slot size array, a running total, and helpers that validate entry sizes, record them, and evict items when the size limit is exceeded.
descriptions.lru-cache-11.3.6/dist/esm/index.js#creat: Given a maximum size, it builds a fixed-capacity stack backed by the smallest suitable unsigned integer typed array, or returns an empty plain array if no such type fits.
descriptions.lru-cache-11.3.6/dist/esm/index.js##evic: It removes the least-recently-used cache entry, aborting pending fetches or running disposal callbacks, optionally freeing its slot for reuse, and returns that entry's slot index.
descriptions.lru-cache-11.3.6/dist/esm/index.js##has@: This takes a key and optional settings, and returns whether the cache holds a fresh, non-pending entry for it. It can also refresh the entry's age and record whether the lookup was a hit, stale, or miss.
descriptions.lru-cache-11.3.6/dist/esm/index.js##set@: It takes a key, a value, and optional settings, then stores or updates the entry in a size-limited, expiring cache, evicting or disposing old items, and returns the cache.
descriptions.lru-cache-11.3.6/dist/esm/index.js##isVa: It takes a numeric position and returns whether it is defined and still valid, meaning the key stored there maps back to that same position in the lookup table.
descriptions.lru-cache-11.3.6/dist/esm/index.js##rind: This generator takes an optional setting for whether expired entries count, then yields cache slot positions from least to most recently used, skipping expired ones unless allowed.
descriptions.lru-cache-11.3.6/dist/esm/index.js##inde: This generator takes an optional setting for including expired entries and yields the cache's internal slot positions from most to least recently used, skipping stale ones unless allowed.
descriptions.lru-cache-11.3.6/dist/esm/index.js##peek: Given a key and options, it looks up the cached value without altering recency, returns undefined if the key is missing or expired (unless stale entries are allowed), and optionally records the outcome.
descriptions.lru-cache-11.3.6/dist/esm/index.js##back: Given a cache key, its slot position, options and context, it starts or reuses an abortable asynchronous fetch. It returns a promise that stores the fetched value, keeps any stale value, and handles aborts and errors.
descriptions.lru-cache-11.3.6/dist/esm/index.js#fetch: Given a fetch error and a continuation flag, it handles a failed cache fetch by deleting or restoring the stale entry, then returns the stale value if permitted or rethrows the error.
descriptions.lru-cache-11.3.6/dist/esm/index.js#eb@12: It takes an error from a rejected fetch, records the rejection and error on an optional status object if present, and returns the result of the fetch-failure handler.
descriptions.lru-cache-11.3.6/dist/esm/index.js##fetc: Given a key and optional settings, it asynchronously returns the cached value if fresh; otherwise it triggers or reuses a background fetch, returning the pending result or a permitted stale value.
descriptions.lru-cache-11.3.6/dist/esm/index.js#fetch: It takes a key and optional settings, attaches status and context for diagnostic tracing when observers are listening, then returns a promise for the asynchronously fetched cache value.
descriptions.lru-cache-11.3.6/dist/esm/index.js##isBa: It takes any value and returns true only if fetching is enabled and the value is a pending background fetch promise carrying a stale value and an abort controller; otherwise false.
descriptions.lru-cache-11.3.6/dist/esm/index.js#cb@11: This callback takes a fetched value and an optional cache-update flag, handles abort status, stores the value, restores the stale value, or deletes the entry, and returns the value or the failure handler's result.
descriptions.lru-cache-11.3.6/dist/esm/index.js#pcall: This promise-executor-style function takes resolve and reject callbacks, starts a cache fetch, and forwards its result or error; on abort it may resolve undefined early and still cache the late result. It returns nothing.
descriptions.lru-cache-11.3.6/dist/esm/index.js#force: Takes a key and optional settings, forces a fresh fetch of that key's value, optionally attaching status and tracing details, and returns a promise for the fetched value.
descriptions.lru-cache-11.3.6/dist/esm/index.js##get@: It takes a key and optional retrieval settings and returns the cached value, marking it recently used. It returns nothing if the entry is missing, or expired when stale results are disallowed.
descriptions.lru-cache-11.3.6/dist/esm/index.js#memo@: It takes a key and optional settings, retrieves or computes a cached value through an internal memoization routine, records diagnostic status for any listening metrics observers, and returns that value.
descriptions.lru-cache-11.3.6/dist/esm/index.js##forc: This asynchronous method takes a key and optional fetch settings, retrieves the associated value through the cache's fetch mechanism, and returns it, throwing an error if no value results.
descriptions.lru-cache-11.3.6/dist/esm/index.js##conn: It takes two node positions and links them in a doubly linked list, making the first precede the second and the second follow the first; it returns nothing.
descriptions.lru-cache-11.3.6/dist/esm/index.js##move: Given a slot position in an index-based doubly linked list, it unlinks that entry and relinks it at the end, marking it most recently used, and returns nothing.
descriptions.lru-cache-11.3.6/dist/esm/index.js##memo: Given a key and optional settings, it returns the cached value when present, otherwise computes one with a configured generator function, stores it, and returns it, optionally recording hit/miss status.

descriptions.nanoid-3.3.12/async/index.cjs#tick@41: <thinking_mode> The constraints are explicit: one sentence, 30 words max, plain prose, and no identifiers from the code — so no "tick", "alphabet", "mask", "step", or "random", only descriptions of what they do. What the function does: it takes a starting string (the id) and a target length, defaulting to some standard size. It asynchronously obtains a batch of random bytes, masks each one, and uses the result as an index into a character set; any byte that lands outside the character set is simply discarded rather than wrapped. Each accepted character is appended to the string, and as soon as the string is long enough, that string is returned. If the batch runs out first, it calls itself again with the partial string and keeps going. So the return is a promise that eventually resolves to a random identifier of the requested length. Key points to fit into one sentence: input is a partial string plus a desired length; mechanism is random bytes mapped to allowed characters with out-of-range bytes rejected, repeating until long enough; output is a promise of the completed ID string. Rejection of out-of-range bytes is worth mentioning since it avoids bias. Wording like "partially built identifier string", "allowed characters", "recursively fetching more bytes as needed", and "promise resolving to the completed random ID" keeps it identifier-free and under 30 words. </thinking_mode> Given a partially built identifier string and a desired length, it asynchronously appends random allowed characters, discarding out-of-range bytes and recursively fetching more, returning a promise resolving to the completed random ID.

descriptions.p-limit-7.3.0/index.js#resumeNext@19: Taking no input and returning nothing, it starts the next waiting task from the queue whenever the number of running tasks is below the allowed concurrency limit.
descriptions.p-limit-7.3.0/index.js#next@27: It takes no arguments and returns nothing. It decrements the count of currently running tasks, then starts the next queued task, freeing a concurrency slot when a task finishes.
descriptions.p-limit-7.3.0/index.js#pLimit@3: Takes a maximum concurrency number (or an options object) and returns a wrapper that queues async tasks so only that many run simultaneously, each call returning a promise of its result.
descriptions.p-limit-7.3.0/index.js#run@32: It takes a task, a resolver callback, and arguments, runs the task asynchronously, immediately passes its promise to the resolver, waits for it to settle, then starts the next queued task.
descriptions.p-limit-7.3.0/index.js#value@78: This takes no input and returns nothing; it empties a queue of pending requests, either silently discarding them or rejecting each with an abort error, depending on configuration.
descriptions.p-limit-7.3.0/index.js#limitFunction@117: It takes a function and concurrency settings, and returns a wrapped version that runs with the same arguments while capping how many calls can execute at once.
descriptions.p-limit-7.3.0/index.js#generator@66: It takes a function and any arguments, queues that call for later execution, and returns a promise that settles with the function's eventual result or error.
descriptions.p-limit-7.3.0/index.js#enqueue@50: It takes a task, its arguments, and the callbacks that settle its result, queues the task to run once a concurrency slot frees up, starts it immediately if one is free, and returns nothing.
descriptions.p-limit-7.3.0/index.js#validateConcurren: It takes a concurrency value and returns nothing, throwing a type error unless the value is a positive integer or positive infinity.
descriptions.p-limit-7.3.0/index.js#value@107: It takes a collection and a callback, schedules the callback on each item and its position through the surrounding concurrency limiter, and returns a promise resolving to all results in order.
descriptions.p-limit-7.3.0/index.js#set@94: This setter takes a new concurrency limit, validates and stores it, then schedules a microtask that starts queued tasks until the limit is reached or the queue empties; it returns nothing.
descriptions.p-throttle-8.1.0/index.js#pThrottle@21: It takes rate-limiting options (call limit, time interval, strict mode, abort signal, delay callback, weighting) and returns a wrapper that makes functions promise-returning and throttled to that rate.
descriptions.p-throttle-8.1.0/index.js#insertTickSort: It takes a timed record and inserts it into a shared, time-ordered list so the list stays sorted, appending quickly when it belongs at the end; it returns nothing.
descriptions.p-throttle-8.1.0/index.js#windowedDelay@: It takes a request's weight, records it against a fixed-window rate limit, and returns how many milliseconds the caller should wait, or zero if it can proceed now.
descriptions.p-throttle-8.1.0/index.js#strictDelay@94: Given a request's weight, it schedules the request under a strict sliding-window rate limit and returns how long to wait, plus the scheduled record when a delay is needed.
descriptions.p-throttle-8.1.0/index.js#get@296: This accessor takes no input and returns how many items are currently waiting in the shared state's queue, read live each time it's accessed.
descriptions.p-throttle-8.1.0/index.js#weightInWindow: Given a point in time, it returns the summed weight of all recorded ticks within a fixed-length window ending at that moment, excluding later ticks and those a full window older.
descriptions.p-throttle-8.1.0/index.js#throttled@174: It takes any arguments, applies rate limiting with optional per-call weights, and returns a promise for the wrapped function's result after any needed delay.

descriptions.semver-7.8.0/classes/comparator.js#Compa: This class takes a version-constraint string, such as an operator followed by a semantic version, and builds an object that tests whether versions satisfy it and whether two constraints overlap.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/classes/comparator.js#inter: This method takes another version constraint and optional matching settings, and returns a boolean saying whether any version could satisfy both constraints at once.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/bin/semver.js#fail@141: This function takes no input and immediately terminates the running program with a failure status code of one, so it never actually returns a value.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/classes/comparator.js#test@: It takes a version, given as a string or parsed object, and returns true if it satisfies the comparator's operator and target version. Wildcards always match, and unparseable strings return false.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/classes/range.js#Range@6: This class takes a semantic version range expression with parsing options and builds a normalized set of alternative constraint groups, supporting formatting, overlap checks with other ranges, and testing whether a version satisfies it.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/classes/comparator.js#toStr: This method takes no arguments and returns the object's stored internal data, so that data serves as the object's string representation whenever it is converted to text.

It extracts the operator, treating an equals sign as none, and the version, using a wildcard if no version is present. It stores both on the object, returns nothing, and throws an error when the string is invalid.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/classes/range.js#format@92: This method takes no arguments and returns the object's stored range value, typically its normalized string form, unchanged.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/classes/range.js#test@193: It takes a version, given as text or as an already-parsed version object, and returns true if it satisfies any of the range's alternative condition groups, otherwise false.

descriptions.semver-7.8.0/classes/range.js#parseRange: It takes a semantic-version range string and returns a cached, deduplicated list of normalized comparator objects, collapsing to a single null-set comparator when the range can never match.

descriptions.semver-7.8.0/classes/range.js#hyphenRepl: Given a flag for including prereleases, it returns a replacer that converts a hyphenated version range into an equivalent pair of lower and upper bound comparators, treating wildcard parts appropriately.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/classes/range.js#replaceGTE: The function takes a version-range comparator string and an options object, trims it, and returns it with any "greater than or equal to zero" comparator removed, honoring the prerelease option.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/classes/range.js#replaceXRa: Takes a version comparator string containing wildcard components plus parsing options, and returns an equivalent explicit range expression with concrete lower and upper version bounds.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/classes/range.js#testSet@52: It takes a list of version constraints, a version, and options, and returns whether the version satisfies every constraint. descriptions.semver-7.8.0/classes/semver.js#compareMa: This method takes another version, either as a version object or as a string it converts, and compares only the major, minor, and patch numbers, returning -1, 0, or 1.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/classes/semver.js#SemVer@9: A class that takes a version string or existing version object, plus parsing options, and returns a validated semantic version object that supports formatting, comparison, and incrementing.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/classes/semver.js#compare@9: It takes another semantic version, either a version object or a string, and returns a negative, zero, or positive number comparing the two, checking main numbers before prerelease tags.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/classes/semver.js#compareBu: This method takes another semantic version, converting it if needed, and compares their build metadata element by element, returning -1, 0, or 1 for less, equal, or greater.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/classes/semver.js#comparePr: It compares this version's pre-release tag against another version's (converting the other to a version object if necessary). It returns negative one, zero, or one, ranking versions without a pre-release tag higher.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/classes/semver.js#format@81: This method takes no arguments. It builds a semantic version string from the object's numeric parts, appending any pre-release tags after a hyphen. It stores the string on the object and returns it.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/classes/semver.js#toString@: This method takes no arguments and returns the object's stored release designation, so the object is represented by that value whenever it is converted to text.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/functions/cmp.js#cmp@10: It takes two version values, a comparison operator string and an optional loose-parsing flag, and returns a boolean for whether the comparison holds, throwing an error for unrecognized operators.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/classes/semver.js#inc@194: Given a release type and optional prerelease label and starting number, it bumps this semantic version accordingly, validating inputs, updating its string form, and returning the modified version object.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/functions/compare-build.js#: It takes two semantic version strings and an optional lenient-parsing flag, and returns a negative, zero, or positive number ordering them, using build metadata to break ties.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/functions/clean.js#clean@4: The function takes a semantic version string plus optional parsing settings, trims whitespace and leading equals signs or "v" prefixes, and returns the normalized version string, or null if it's invalid.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/functions/coerce.js#coerce@: It takes a loosely formatted version value, such as a string or number, and extracts a semantic version from it. It returns a parsed version object, or null if nothing usable is found.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/functions/diff.js#diff@5: It takes two semantic version strings and returns the kind of release change between them, such as major, minor, patch, a pre-prefixed variant, or prerelease, or null if they are equal.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/functions/gt.js#gt@4: It takes two version values and an optional leniency flag, compares them, and returns true if the first is strictly greater than the second, otherwise false.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/functions/compare-loose.js#: This function takes two version strings and returns a negative, zero, or positive number showing their order, using lenient parsing that tolerates loosely formatted versions.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/functions/eq.js#eq@4: This function takes two values, typically version strings, plus an optional leniency flag, and returns true if a comparison finds them equal, otherwise false.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/functions/compare.js#compar: It takes two version strings and an optional leniency flag, parses both as semantic versions, and returns negative one, zero, or one depending on which is greater.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/functions/gte.js#gte@4: This function takes two version values and an optional leniency flag, compares them, and returns true if the first is greater than or equal to the second.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/functions/inc.js#inc@5: It takes a semantic version, a release type to bump, and optional parsing options and prerelease labels, and returns the incremented version string, or null if invalid.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/functions/lt.js#lt@4: This function takes two version values and an optional flag for lenient parsing, compares them, and returns true if the first version is strictly lower than the second.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/functions/lte.js#lte@4: It takes two version values and an optional flag for lenient parsing, and returns true if the first version is less than or equal to the second.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/functions/neq.js#neq@4: It takes two values, likely version strings, plus an optional leniency flag, and returns true when a comparison finds them unequal, otherwise false.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/functions/major.js#major@4: It takes a version string and an optional lenient-parsing flag, parses the string as a semantic version, and returns its leading version number as an integer.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/functions/rcompare.js#rcomp: It takes two version strings and an optional leniency flag, compares them in reverse order, and returns a negative, zero, or positive number for descending sorting.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/functions/minor.js#minor@4: It takes a version string and an optional leniency flag, parses the string as a semantic version, and returns its second numeric component, the middle number.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/functions/parse.js#parse@4: It takes a version value, optional parsing settings, and an error-handling flag, and returns a semantic version object, either the input unchanged or newly parsed, or null when parsing fails unless errors should be raised.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/functions/patch.js#patch@4: It takes a version string and an optional flag for lenient parsing, parses it as a semantic version, and returns its third numeric component, the bug-fix number.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/functions/rsort.js#rsort@4: It takes a list of version strings and a flag for lenient parsing, sorts the list in place from newest to oldest (using build metadata to break ties), and returns it.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/functions/satisfies.js#sati: It takes a version, a version range, and optional parsing settings, and returns true if the version falls within the range, or false if not or if the range is invalid.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/functions/sort.js#sort@4: It takes a list of version strings and an optional lenient-parsing flag, sorts the list in place in ascending version order (using build metadata to break ties), and returns it.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/functions/prerelease.js#pre: It takes a semantic release string and optional parsing settings, and returns the list of hyphen-suffixed tag components if any exist, otherwise nothing when absent or invalid.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/functions/truncate.js#trunc: It takes a version, a release-level name, and parsing options, and returns a copy of the version truncated to that level, or null if the level or version is invalid.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/functions/truncate.js#isPre: It takes a version-change type label and returns true if the label begins with "pre", indicating a prerelease variant, otherwise false.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/functions/truncate.js#doTru: Given a semantic version object and a truncation level, it returns the version string unchanged for prerelease levels, otherwise strips prerelease tags and zeroes the lower-order numbers.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/functions/truncate.js#clone: It takes a semantic version, either as an existing version object or a string, plus parsing options, and returns a freshly parsed copy of that version.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/internal/identifiers.js#com: It takes two version identifiers and returns negative one, zero, or one, comparing them numerically when both look numeric, ranking numeric before non-numeric, and otherwise comparing as text.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/internal/identifiers.js#rco: This function takes two version identifiers and returns their comparison in reverse order: negative, zero, or positive, so sorting with it puts them in descending order.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/internal/lrucache.js#get@9: Given a key, it returns the stored value or nothing if absent, and marks found entries as most recently used by moving them to the end, as in a least-recently-used cache.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/internal/lrucache.js#delete: This method takes a lookup value, removes its matching entry from the object's internal collection, and returns true if an entry was found and removed, otherwise false.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/internal/lrucache.js#LRUCac: This is a bounded cache of up to a thousand key-value pairs that evicts the least recently used entry, returns stored values on lookup, and oddly removes existing keys when they are re-stored.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/functions/valid.js#valid@4: It takes a candidate semantic-versioning string plus optional parsing settings, and returns the normalized form if it parses correctly, or null if it is malformed.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/internal/parse-options.js#p: <thinking>Need one sentence, no identifiers.</thinking>It takes an optional settings value and returns a default empty configuration if missing, a preset permissive configuration if it isn't an object, or otherwise the original object unchanged.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/internal/lrucache.js#set@25: Given a key and value, it removes the key if already present; otherwise it stores a defined value, evicting the oldest entry when full, and returns the cache itself.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/internal/re.js#makeSafeRege: It takes a regular expression pattern string and returns it with unbounded star and plus repetitions on certain tokens replaced by capped ranges, preventing catastrophic backtracking.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/ranges/intersects.js#inters: It takes two version range specifications plus optional parsing settings, normalizes both into range objects, and returns a boolean indicating whether any version could satisfy both ranges.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/ranges/gtr.js#gtr@5: It takes a version, a version range, and optional settings, and returns true if the version is greater than every version the range could match, otherwise false.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/ranges/max-satisfying.js#ma: It takes a list of version strings and a version range, and returns the highest version that satisfies the range, or nothing if the range is invalid or nothing matches.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/ranges/min-satisfying.js#mi: It takes a list of version strings, a version range, and parsing options, and returns the lowest version that satisfies the range, or null if none match or the range is invalid.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/ranges/ltr.js#ltr@5: It takes a version, a version range, and optional settings, and returns true if the version is lower than every version the range could match, otherwise false.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/ranges/min-version.js#minVe: Given a semantic version range and an optional lenient-parsing flag, it returns the lowest version satisfying that range, or null if no such version exists.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/internal/re.js#createToken@: It takes a token name, a regex pattern string, and a global flag, and registers it under a new index with its pattern and compiled regular and safe regexes; returns nothing.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/ranges/outside.js#outside@1: Takes a version, a version range, a direction (greater-than or less-than), and options; returns true if the version lies entirely beyond the range in that direction, otherwise false.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/ranges/subset.js#subset@45: It takes two version range specifications plus optional parsing settings and returns a boolean indicating whether every version satisfying the first range also satisfies the second.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/ranges/subset.js#simpleSubs: It takes two sets of version comparators plus options and decides whether every version matching the first set also matches the second. It returns true or false, or null if the first set matches nothing.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/ranges/subset.js#higherGT@2: Given two lower-bound version comparators and comparison options, it returns the stricter one: the higher version, or the exclusive bound on a tie, or the second if the first is missing.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/ranges/to-comparators.js#to: It takes a version range expression and parsing options, and returns a list of alternative sets, each containing the individual comparator strings that make up that set.
descriptions.toposort-2.0.2/index.js#toposort@37: It takes a list of nodes and a list of directed edges between them, and returns the nodes in topologically sorted order. It throws an error on cycles or unknown nodes.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/ranges/subset.js#lowerLT@23: Given two upper-bound version constraints, where the first may be missing, it returns the more restrictive one: the lower version, or the strict "less than" bound when versions tie.
descriptions.toposort-2.0.2/index.js#makeOutgoingEdge: It takes a list of directed edges given as pairs and returns a map from every node to the set of nodes it points to, with nodes lacking outgoing edges mapped to empty sets.
descriptions.toposort-2.0.2/index.js#makeNodesHash@11: It takes an array and returns a map from each element to its index position; if an element appears more than once, its last index wins.
descriptions.toposort-2.0.2/index.js#visit@59: This recursive depth-first step of a topological sort takes a node, its index and the set of nodes on the current path, visits its dependents, then places the node into the sorted output from the end, returning nothing. It throws an error if it finds a cycle or an unknown node.
descriptions.toposort-2.0.2/index.js#uniqueNodes@93: It takes a list of edges, each a pair of endpoints, and returns an array of every distinct endpoint in order of first appearance.
descriptions.semver-7.8.0/ranges/valid.js#validRange@: It takes a version range expression and parsing options, and returns the normalized range string (a wildcard if it is empty) or null if the range is invalid.
descriptions.uuid-11.1.1/dist/cjs/parse.js#parse@4: It takes a standard hyphenated unique-identifier string, rejects it with an error if it is malformed, and returns its sixteen bytes as an array.
descriptions.uuid-11.1.1/dist/cjs/md5.js#md5@4: It takes input data as a byte array, string (encoded as UTF-8), or buffer, and returns its MD5 hash as a raw binary buffer.
descriptions.uuid-11.1.1/dist/cjs/rng.js#rng@6: This takes no arguments and returns 16 cryptographically secure random bytes, drawn from a shared buffer that is refilled with fresh random data whenever it runs low.
descriptions.uuid-11.1.1/dist/cjs/sha1.js#sha1@4: It takes input data as a byte array, text string, or binary buffer, normalizes it to a buffer, and returns the raw SHA-1 hash digest as a buffer.
descriptions.uuid-11.1.1/dist/cjs/stringify.js#unsafe: It takes an array of bytes and an optional starting position, and returns the sixteen bytes there formatted as a lowercase, hyphen-separated UUID string, without any validation.
descriptions.uuid-11.1.1/dist/cjs/v1.js#v1@7: It takes optional generation settings plus an optional output buffer and position, produces a time-based version 1 unique identifier, and returns the filled buffer or the identifier as a string.
descriptions.uuid-11.1.1/dist/cjs/uuid-bin.js#usage@1: It takes no input and returns nothing; it prints command-line help showing how to generate each supported unique-identifier version, plus a note on the predefined web-address and domain-name namespace shortcuts.
descriptions.uuid-11.1.1/dist/cjs/v1ToV6.js#v1ToV6@5: It converts a version-1 UUID, given as a string or byte array, into the equivalent version-6 UUID, returning it in the same format it was given.
descriptions.uuid-11.1.1/dist/cjs/stringify.js#string: It takes a byte array and an optional starting position, converts sixteen bytes into a standard UUID string, and returns it, throwing an error if the result is invalid.
descriptions.uuid-11.1.1/dist/cjs/v1.js#updateV1State: Given a mutable timestamp-based identifier generator state, the current time in milliseconds, and random bytes, it updates the sub-millisecond counter, regenerating node and clock sequence when needed, then returns the state.
descriptions.uuid-11.1.1/dist/cjs/v1.js#v1Bytes@52: This function takes random bytes plus optional timestamp, clock sequence, node identifier, and target buffer, and returns a 16-byte buffer containing a version-1 time-based UUID.
descriptions.uuid-11.1.1/dist/cjs/v1ToV6.js#_v1ToV6@1: It takes the 16 bytes of a version-1 UUID and returns a new 16-byte array for the equivalent version-6 UUID. The timestamp fields are reordered so the most significant parts come first, the version marker is set to 6, and the remaining bytes are copied unchanged.
descriptions.uuid-11.1.1/dist/cjs/v35.js#v35@17: It takes a version number, hash function, name, namespace and optional output buffer with offset, and returns a name-based UUID. The result is either a formatted string or the buffer filled with its 16 bytes.
descriptions.uuid-11.1.1/dist/cjs/v3.js#v3@9: This function generates a version 3 name-based UUID by MD5-hashing a name within a namespace, returning it as a string or writing its bytes into an optional buffer at an offset.
descriptions.uuid-11.1.1/dist/cjs/v5.js#v5@9: It takes a name, a namespace identifier, and optionally an output buffer and offset. It returns a version 5 UUID, made by SHA-1 hashing the namespace and name, either as a string or written into the buffer.
descriptions.uuid-11.1.1/dist/cjs/v4.js#v4@6: This generates a random version-4 UUID from optional settings, random bytes, or a supplied generator, returning it as a string or writing its sixteen bytes into a provided buffer at an offset.
descriptions.uuid-11.1.1/dist/cjs/v35.js#stringToByte: It takes a text string, encodes it as UTF-8, and returns the resulting sequence of bytes as an array of unsigned 8-bit integers.
descriptions.uuid-11.1.1/dist/cjs/v6.js#v6@6: It generates a time-ordered version 6 UUID from optional settings, then either writes its sixteen bytes into a supplied buffer at an offset or returns it as a string.
descriptions.uuid-11.1.1/dist/cjs/v6ToV1.js#v6ToV1@5: It takes a version 6 UUID, either as a string or a byte array, and returns the equivalent version 1 UUID in the same format.
descriptions.uuid-11.1.1/dist/cjs/v7.js#v7@7: It generates a time-ordered version 7 UUID from optional settings, an output buffer and a position, returning that filled buffer if one was supplied, otherwise the UUID as a string.
descriptions.uuid-11.1.1/dist/cjs/v7.js#v7Bytes@36: Given random bytes, an optional millisecond timestamp, a sequence counter and an output buffer, it writes a 16-byte version-7 UUID and returns the filled buffer.
descriptions.uuid-11.1.1/dist/cjs/v7.js#updateV7State: It takes a mutable generator state, the current timestamp in milliseconds and random bytes, and returns that state updated for time-ordered identifiers. A newer timestamp reseeds the sequence counter from the random bytes; otherwise the counter increments, advancing the stored timestamp on overflow.
descriptions.uuid-11.1.1/dist/cjs-browser/md5.js#uint: It takes an array of 32-bit unsigned integers and returns a byte array four times as long, splitting each integer into its four bytes in little-endian order.
descriptions.uuid-11.1.1/dist/cjs/v6ToV1.js#_v6ToV1@1: It takes the 16 bytes of a version-6 UUID and returns a new byte array holding the equivalent version-1 UUID, with the timestamp bits reordered and the version marker changed.
descriptions.uuid-11.1.1/dist/cjs/version.js#version@: It takes a UUID string, checks that it is valid (throwing an error if not), and returns its version number from the hexadecimal digit at the version position.
descriptions.uuid-11.1.1/dist/cjs/validate.js#validat: This function takes a value and returns true only if it is a string matching a predefined pattern for a universally unique identifier, otherwise false.
descriptions.uuid-11.1.1/dist/cjs-browser/md5.js#safe: It takes two numbers and returns their sum wrapped to a signed 32-bit integer, adding the low and high 16-bit halves separately to avoid precision problems.
descriptions.uuid-11.1.1/dist/cjs-browser/md5.js#md5@: It takes a byte array, computes its MD5 hash over the full bit length, and returns the resulting digest as a byte array.
descriptions.uuid-11.1.1/dist/cjs-browser/md5.js#uint: It takes an array of bytes and returns an array of 32-bit unsigned integers, packing every four bytes into one word in little-endian order and sizing the output from the input's bit length.
descriptions.uuid-11.1.1/dist/cjs-browser/md5.js#bitR: It takes a 32-bit integer and a shift amount, and returns the integer with its bits rotated left by that amount, wrapping overflowed high bits around to the low end.
descriptions.uuid-11.1.1/dist/cjs-browser/md5.js#getO: Given a message length in bits, it returns how many 32-bit words the padded message buffer needs, up to and including the length slot, as in MD5-style hashing.
descriptions.uuid-11.1.1/dist/cjs-browser/md5.js#word: It takes an array of little-endian 32-bit words and a message length in bits, pads the message, and computes its MD5 digest, returning four 32-bit words.
descriptions.uuid-11.1.1/dist/cjs-browser/md5.js#md5f: It performs one first-round step of the MD5 hash: given four state words, a message word, a shift amount and a constant, it returns the updated 32-bit state value.
descriptions.uuid-11.1.1/dist/cjs-browser/md5.js#md5g: It performs one second-round step of the MD5 hash: given four state words, a message word, a shift amount and a constant, it mixes them and returns the updated 32-bit word.
descriptions.uuid-11.1.1/dist/cjs-browser/md5.js#md5c: This core step of the MD5 round takes six 32-bit integers, adds four of them, rotates the sum left by a given amount, adds another value, and returns the 32-bit result.
descriptions.uuid-11.1.1/dist/cjs-browser/md5.js#md5h: This performs one step of the MD5 hash's third round: it takes four state words, a message word, a shift amount and a constant, and returns the updated state word.
descriptions.uuid-11.1.1/dist/cjs-browser/md5.js#md5i: This MD5 fourth-round helper takes four state words, a message word, a shift amount and a constant, applies the round's nonlinear mixing function, and returns the updated 32-bit state word.
descriptions.uuid-11.1.1/dist/cjs-browser/rng.js#rng@: It takes no arguments and returns a reused 16-byte buffer of cryptographically secure random bytes, setting up the system random source on first use and throwing an error if none exists.
descriptions.uuid-11.1.1/dist/cjs-browser/sha1.js#f@3: Given a round-stage selector (0–3) and three 32-bit words, it returns the corresponding SHA-1 logical function: choose for stage 0, majority for stage 2, and three-way XOR for stages 1 and 3.
descriptions.uuid-11.1.1/dist/cjs-browser/sha1.js#ROT: It takes a 32-bit integer and a shift count, and returns the integer's bits rotated left by that many positions, with bits shifted off the top wrapping around to the bottom.
descriptions.uuid-11.1.1/dist/cjs-browser/sha1.js#sha: It takes a sequence of raw bytes and returns their 20-byte SHA-1 cryptographic hash digest as a new byte array.
descriptions.uuid-11.1.1/dist/esm/md5.js#md5@2: This function takes binary data, an array of byte values, or a text string (encoded as UTF-8) and returns its MD5 hash as a raw binary buffer.
descriptions.uuid-11.1.1/dist/esm/stringify.js#unsafe: It takes an array of bytes and an optional starting position, and returns the sixteen bytes there as a lowercase, hyphenated UUID string, without validating the input.
descriptions.uuid-11.1.1/dist/esm/parse.js#parse@2: It takes a UUID string, checks that it is valid (throwing a type error if not), and returns its sixteen bytes as an unsigned byte array.
descriptions.uuid-11.1.1/dist/esm/rng.js#rng@4: Taking no arguments, it returns sixteen cryptographically random bytes, sliced from a shared pre-filled buffer that is refilled with fresh random data whenever too few unused bytes remain.
descriptions.uuid-11.1.1/dist/esm/sha1.js#sha1@2: It takes binary data, an array of byte values, or a text string (encoded as UTF-8), and returns the raw SHA-1 hash of that input as a binary buffer.
descriptions.uuid-11.1.1/dist/esm/v1.js#updateV1State: This takes a version-1 UUID generator's state, the current timestamp and random bytes, and returns that state updated in place. It advances the sub-millisecond counter and regenerates the node identifier and clock sequence when time goes backward or the counter overflows.
descriptions.uuid-11.1.1/dist/esm/v1.js#v1@4: This function generates a time-based version 1 UUID from optional settings, an optional buffer and an offset. It returns the filled buffer if one was given, otherwise the UUID as a string.
descriptions.uuid-11.1.1/dist/esm/v35.js#stringToByte: It takes a text string and returns its UTF-8 encoding as an array of unsigned 8-bit byte values.
descriptions.uuid-11.1.1/dist/esm/stringify.js#string: This function takes a byte array and an optional starting position, converts sixteen bytes into a standard UUID string, and returns it, throwing an error if the result is invalid.
descriptions.uuid-11.1.1/dist/esm/v1ToV6.js#v1ToV6@3: The function takes a version-1 universally unique identifier, as text or raw bytes, reorders it into the version-6 layout, and returns it in the same format it received.
descriptions.uuid-11.1.1/dist/esm/v35.js#v35@13: It builds a name-based version 3 or 5 UUID by hashing a namespace and a name. It returns the result as a formatted string, or writes the sixteen bytes into a supplied buffer at an offset.
descriptions.uuid-11.1.1/dist/esm/v4.js#v4@4: It takes optional settings, an optional output buffer, and an optional starting position, and returns a random version-4 identifier, either as a string or written into that buffer.
descriptions.uuid-11.1.1/dist/esm/v3.js#v3@4: It produces a version-3 universally unique identifier by MD5-hashing a name within a namespace, returning it as a string or writing its bytes into an optional buffer at a given position.
descriptions.uuid-11.1.1/dist/esm/v6.js#v6@4: It generates a reordered time-based unique identifier from optional settings, writing its sixteen bytes into a supplied buffer at an offset and returning the buffer, or else returning a string.
descriptions.uuid-11.1.1/dist/esm/v7.js#v7@4: This function generates a time-ordered version 7 UUID from optional settings (custom randomness, timestamp, sequence) and returns it as a string, or writes it into a supplied buffer at an offset and returns that buffer.
descriptions.uuid-11.1.1/dist/esm/v6ToV1.js#v6ToV1@3: It converts a version-6 UUID, given as a string or byte array, into its version-1 equivalent and returns it in the same form as the input.
descriptions.uuid-11.1.1/dist/esm/v5.js#v5@4: It generates a version-5 name-based UUID by SHA-1 hashing a name within a namespace UUID, returning the UUID as a string or writing it into an optional buffer at an offset.
descriptions.validator-13.15.35/index.js#_interopRequ: It takes an imported module and returns it unchanged if it is already marked as an ES module; otherwise it wraps the value in an object as the default export.
descriptions.uuid-11.1.1/dist/esm/v7.js#updateV7State: Given a mutable generator state, the current millisecond timestamp, and random bytes, it updates the state for time-ordered unique IDs, reseeding the counter when time advances or incrementing it otherwise, and returns the state.
descriptions.uuid-11.1.1/dist/esm/validate.js#validat: The function takes a value and returns true only if it is a string matching a predefined pattern for a universally unique identifier; otherwise it returns false.
descriptions.uuid-11.1.1/dist/esm-browser/rng.js#rng@: Taking no arguments, it fills a shared byte buffer with cryptographically secure random values and returns it, throwing an error if the environment lacks secure randomness support.
descriptions.validator-13.15.35/index.js#_typeof@3: It takes any value and returns a string naming its type, like the built-in type operator, but correctly reports polyfilled symbols as "symbol" in environments without native symbol support.
descriptions.validator-13.15.35/lib/equals.js#equals@: It takes an input string and a comparison value, verifies the input is a string, and returns true only if they are strictly identical, otherwise false.
descriptions.validator-13.15.35/lib/blacklist.js#blac: This function takes an input string and a set of characters, checks that the input is a string, and returns a copy with every occurrence of those characters removed.
descriptions.uuid-11.1.1/dist/esm/version.js#version@: It takes a universally unique identifier string, checks that it is well-formed (throwing an error otherwise), and returns its generation-scheme number, read from one specific hexadecimal digit.
descriptions.validator-13.15.35/lib/isAbaRouting.js#i: It takes a string and returns true only if it is a properly formatted American bank routing number whose digits pass the weighted 3-7-1 checksum, otherwise false.
descriptions.validator-13.15.35/index.js#_interopRequ: It takes a loaded module and an optional flag, and returns an ES-module-style namespace object: the module unchanged if already ES, otherwise a cached wrapper copying its properties with the original as the default export.
descriptions.validator-13.15.35/lib/escape.js#escape@: It takes a string, checks that it really is a string, and returns a copy with HTML-sensitive characters (ampersands, quotes, angle brackets, slashes, backslashes, backticks) replaced by their HTML entity equivalents.
descriptions.validator-13.15.35/lib/contains.js#conta: It takes a string, a search value, and optional settings, and returns true if the string contains that value at least a minimum number of times, optionally ignoring case.
descriptions.validator-13.15.35/lib/isAlpha.js#isAlph: It takes a string, an optional locale (default US English) and optional characters to ignore, and returns whether the remaining string contains only letters of that locale's alphabet.
descriptions.validator-13.15.35/lib/isAfter.js#isAfte: It takes a date string and an optional reference date, defaulting to now, and returns true only if both parse as valid dates and the first falls strictly later.
