descriptions.validator-13.15.35/lib/util/nullUndefine: This function takes any single value and returns a boolean that is true only when the value is explicitly empty or entirely unset, and false otherwise.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/ZodError.ts#quoteless: It takes any value, converts it to an indented, pretty-printed JSON string, and returns that string with the quotation marks around property names removed.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/ZodError.ts#format@21: It takes a function that converts each validation issue into a custom value, and returns a nested error object mirroring the schema's shape, with those converted values grouped at each level.

It takes an optional function for transforming each validation problem and returns a nested object mirroring the data's shape, with every field holding its error messages, including those from unions and function signatures.
This method takes no arguments and returns the validation errors as a nested object that mirrors the shape of the validated data, with error messages attached at each level.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/ZodError.ts#processEr: It takes a validation error and recursively walks its issues, including nested union, return-type, and argument errors, mapping each message into a shared nested object keyed by path; it returns nothing.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/ZodError.ts#ZodError@: This error class wraps a list of validation issues and provides ways to inspect, add, and reshape them into nested or flattened per-field error message structures.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/ZodError.ts#toString@: This method takes no arguments and returns the object's stored message text as its string representation, overriding the default conversion inherited from its parent class.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/ZodError.ts#flatten@2: This method optionally takes a function that transforms each validation issue, and returns a simplified error object separating top-level form errors from per-field error lists.
This function takes no arguments, increments a counter variable defined outside it, and returns the counter's new value.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/ZodError.ts#assert@27: It takes any value and returns nothing, throwing an error if the value isn't the library's validation-error type, so callers can then treat it as that type.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/ZodError.ts#flatten@2: This method takes no arguments and returns a simplified view of a validation error, splitting messages into top-level form errors and per-field errors keyed by field name.
This function takes no arguments. It increments an external counter and returns the counter's remainder after division by one hundred, written as a hexadecimal string.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/ZodError.ts#flatten@2: It takes an optional transform for each validation issue (defaulting to its message) and returns top-level errors plus errors grouped by the first segment of each issue's path.
The function takes a zero-argument generator and returns a list of freshly generated values whose length (zero to nine) is set by an external counter, which it increments on each call.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/errors.ts#setErrorMap: It takes a custom validation error-message mapping and installs it as the global override for formatting errors, returning nothing.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/helpers/errorUtil.ts#: It takes an optional error message, either plain text or an object with a message field, and returns that text, or nothing if no message is given.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/benchmarks/string.ts#: It accepts a value of any type, returns it unchanged if it is text, and otherwise throws an exception saying the input isn't text.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/errors.ts#getErrorMap: This function takes no arguments and returns the currently active custom error-message mapping, which is stored at module level and may have been overridden by the user.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/helpers/parseUtil.ts#: This class tracks a validation state (valid, dirty, or aborted) and combines individual parse results into an array or object, returning an invalid result if any part aborted.

It takes a parsing context and validation issue details, builds a complete issue with its message resolved through prioritized error maps, and appends it to the context's issue list, returning nothing.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/helpers/errorUtil.ts#: It takes an optional error message, either plain text or an object with a message, and returns an object containing that message, or an empty object if none.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/helpers/parseUtil.ts#: This function takes input data, a location path, a list of message-generating handlers, and partial issue details, and returns a complete validation issue with a combined path and resolved error message.
It takes an overall parse status and a list of individual parse results, then returns a combined result with their values collected into an array, or an invalid marker if any was aborted.
It takes a parse-status tracker and a list of parsed key-value results, then returns a combined object with the overall status, or an invalid marker if any entry aborted.
This method takes no arguments and returns nothing; it marks the object's state as aborted, changing it only if it isn't already in that state.
It takes a value of any type and returns an object that wraps that value alongside a status marker flagging it as invalid or tainted.
This type guard takes a parsing result and returns true if its status marks it as aborted, narrowing its type to the invalid-result type.
This function takes any single input and returns an object wrapping it alongside a marker indicating success, producing a typed success result for validation or parsing workflows.
It takes a parsing result and reports whether its status is marked as "dirty," and it also narrows the result's type to successful or dirty outcomes for the compiler.
This method takes no arguments and returns nothing; it downgrades the object's status from approved to modified, but only if it is currently in the approved state.
It takes a parsing result and returns true if promises exist in the environment and that result is a promise, marking it as an asynchronous parse result.

<thinking_mode>auto</thinking_mode> It takes a parse status and a list of possibly asynchronous key-value parse results, awaits each in order, then returns a promise of the merged synchronous object parse result.
This type guard takes a parsing result and returns true when its status is valid, letting the type system treat the result as a successful one from then on.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/helpers/util.ts#array: It takes a non-empty list of strings and returns an object where each string is both a key and its own value, like an enum.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/helpers/util.ts#asser: This function takes a value the type system says can never exist, used for exhaustiveness checks, and never returns because it always throws an error when called.
It accepts a single value whose type only checks when two type parameters are identical, acting as a compile-time type-equality assertion, and returns nothing while doing nothing at runtime.
This function accepts a single value of a specified generic type, does nothing at runtime, and returns nothing; it exists only to make the compiler verify the value's type.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/helpers/util.ts#find@: It takes an array and a test function, then returns the first element that passes the test, or undefined if none does.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/helpers/util.ts#getVa: The function takes a TypeScript enum object, filters out the reverse-mapping entries that numeric enums generate, and returns an array of the enum's actual member values.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/helpers/util.ts#objec: This function takes an object and returns an array of its property values, ordered by the keys a helper function supplies, similar to the built-in way of listing an object's values.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/helpers/util.ts#joinV: It takes an array and an optional separator (a vertical bar by default), wraps string elements in single quotes, and returns all elements joined into one string.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/helpers/util.ts#jsonS: This serialization helper takes a property key and its value, returning big integers converted to their string form and leaving every other value unchanged.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/helpers/util.ts#merge: It takes two objects and returns a new object combining both sets of properties, with values from the second object overriding any matching properties from the first.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/tests/Mocker.ts#getRa: It takes a maximum number, rounds it down, and returns a random whole number from zero up to, but not including, that rounded-down maximum.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/locales/en.ts#errorMa: Takes a schema validation issue and its context, and returns an object holding a human-readable English error message matched to the issue's kind and details.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/tests/async-parsing.t: This function accepts no inputs, performs no operations, and returns nothing, serving only as an empty placeholder.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/helpers/util.ts#getPa: It takes any value and returns a detailed type category for it, distinguishing primitives, not-a-number, null, arrays, promise-like objects, maps, sets, dates, plain objects, and unknown.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/tests/async-parsing.t: It takes an optional flag for asynchronous validation and returns a validation schema for an object with a text field and a nested number field whose check always fails.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/tests/Mocker.ts#Mocke: This class takes no input and produces random test values on demand: strings, numbers, big integers, booleans, dates, a fixed symbol, null, undefined, and randomly optional or nullable variants.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/tests/branded.test.ts: This function takes a single value matching a specific schema type and returns that same value unchanged, acting as a typed identity or pass-through helper.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/tests/catch.test.ts#c: This function takes no arguments, sets an outside flag to mark that it has been called, and returns a fixed short placeholder string.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/tests/base.test.ts#ca: This function takes a test function that judges a piece of text and returns that test's true-or-false verdict on the fixed word "hello".
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/tests/error.test.ts#e: This custom validation error formatter receives an error, asserts in a test that its location path has exactly two segments, and returns a placeholder message object.

It takes a validation issue and its context, then returns a custom message: a "bad type" note for wrong-type errors where text was expected, a minimum-based message for custom issues, or the default error otherwise.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/tests/function.test.t: This function takes no inputs and returns nothing; it calls another routine with an object holding a number, a string and a list of booleans, apparently to test invalid input.
This function takes no arguments and calls another function with a deliberately invalid string, bypassing type checks, likely to test error handling; it returns nothing.
This function takes no arguments and invokes a validation routine on a sample object containing a number, a string, and a list of booleans, returning nothing.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/tests/instanceof.test: This isn't actually a function: it's an empty class declaration with no fields or methods, so it takes no inputs and returns nothing.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/tests/generics.test.t: It takes a validation schema and an unknown value, validates the value by wrapping it in a temporary container object, and asynchronously returns the validated, unwrapped result.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/tests/optional.test.t: Given a validation schema and an invalid value, this test helper checks that the optional version of the schema reports the same flattened errors as the original, returning nothing.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/tests/instanceof.test: This is a class rather than a function: an abstract base whose constructor takes a string and stores it as a public property, yielding subclass instances since it can't be instantiated directly.
This isn't a function but an empty class declaration that inherits everything from its parent abstract class without adding anything, so it takes no inputs and returns nothing.
This is a class declaration, not a function: it defines an empty subclass that inherits all behavior and constructor parameters from its parent test class unchanged, adding nothing new.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/tests/nullable.test.t: This test helper takes a validation schema and an invalid value, then checks that the nullable version of the schema produces the same flattened errors as the original; it returns nothing.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/tests/pickomit.test.t: This function takes no input and validates an object whose name field is a number instead of text, so it most likely throws a validation error rather than returning anything.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/tests/object-augmenta: This takes no input and validates a hard-coded animal record (a nonsense species name and a population number) against a modified animal schema. It returns the parsed result, but is presumably meant to throw a validation error.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/tests/pickomit.test.t: This function takes no arguments and attempts to validate an object whose name field is a number instead of text, returning the parsed result or, more likely, throwing a validation error.
This function takes no input and validates a fish-like object containing only an age of twelve against a schema, returning the parsed result or likely throwing a validation error.

This function takes no arguments and validates an object containing only an age of twelve against a schema expecting just a name, returning the parsed result or, more likely, throwing a validation error.
This function takes no arguments; it validates a hardcoded object with a name and an extra age field against a name-only schema, returning the parsed result or throwing an error.
This function takes no input and validates an empty object against a predefined fish schema, returning the parsed result or, more likely, throwing a validation error for the missing fields.
It takes no input, runs a validation schema's parser on a hard-coded object with a name and an age (bypassing type checks), and returns the parsed result or throws if validation fails.

This function takes no arguments and validates a deliberately malformed object containing an empty nested object against a schema, returning the parsed result or, more likely, throwing a validation error.
This function takes no arguments and attempts to validate a deliberately malformed object with a schema parser, returning the parsed result or, more likely, throwing a validation error.
This function takes no input and validates a hardcoded string against a schema expecting one specific literal value, returning the string on a match or likely throwing a validation error otherwise.

This function takes no arguments and validates the boolean value true against a schema expecting a specific literal string. It returns the parsed result, though it will most likely throw a validation error.
This function takes no arguments, checks the fixed number thirteen against a schema for an exact numeric value, and returns the validated number or throws an error if validation fails.
This function takes no arguments and validates the number 123 against a schema expecting a specific literal string, so it most likely throws a validation error instead of returning anything.
This function takes no arguments; it validates a captured string value against a numeric-literal schema and returns the parsed result, throwing an error if validation fails.
This function takes no arguments; it validates a boolean property from an outside object against a schema expecting a specific number, returning the parsed value or throwing a validation error.
This function takes no arguments, validates the boolean value false against a predefined literal-boolean schema, and returns the parsed result (false) or throws an error if validation fails.
This function takes no arguments and validates the number 123 against a schema expecting a specific boolean literal, so it almost certainly throws a validation error instead of returning anything.
This function takes no input and validates the string "asdf" against a schema expecting a specific big-integer literal, which would normally throw a validation error instead of returning a value.
It takes no arguments, validates an empty object against a schema expecting a literal string, and returns the parsed result, though it will most likely throw a validation error.
This function takes no input and validates an empty object against a schema expecting a specific boolean value; since an empty object never matches, it always throws a validation error.
This function takes no arguments, checks the big-integer value forty-three against a schema expecting a specific literal big integer, and returns that value if valid, otherwise throwing an error.
This takes no input and validates the fixed text "asdf" against a schema expecting a specific literal boolean; validation will almost certainly fail, so it throws an error rather than returning.

This function takes no arguments, checks the number 123 against a schema expecting a specific big-integer literal, and returns the validated value, or throws a validation error since a plain number likely fails.
This function takes no input, validates an undefined property of an existing object against a string schema, and returns the parsed string, throwing an error if validation fails.
This function takes no arguments, validates a property of an outer object against a string schema, and returns the validated string or throws an error if validation fails.
This function takes no input and validates an empty object against a schema expecting a specific big integer literal, so it almost certainly throws a validation error instead of returning anything.
This function takes no arguments, validates a number-named property of an outside object against a string schema, and returns the parsed string or throws a validation error if invalid.
This function takes no arguments; it validates a stored string value against a numeric schema and returns the parsed number, throwing an error if validation fails.
This function takes no arguments; it validates a boolean-named property of an outer object against a string validation schema, returning the value if it is a valid string and throwing otherwise.
This function takes no arguments, validates a boolean field from an outer object against a numeric schema, and returns the parsed number, or throws an error if validation fails.
This function takes no arguments, checks a big-integer property of an outside object against a numeric validation schema, and returns the validated value or throws if validation fails.
This function takes no arguments, validates a particular property of an outer object against a numeric validation schema, and returns the parsed number, throwing an error if validation fails.
This function takes no arguments and validates a null-valued property from an outer object against a big-integer schema, returning the parsed result or throwing if validation fails.
This function takes no arguments, checks a particular property of an outside object against a numeric validation schema, and returns the validated number, throwing an error if validation fails.
This function takes no arguments; it validates a number property from an outer value against a big-integer schema and returns the parsed result, throwing an error if validation fails.

This function takes no arguments and validates an undefined value against a big-integer schema, returning the parsed result or, more likely, throwing a validation error because undefined is not a big integer.
This function takes no arguments, validates a string held in an outer variable against a big-integer schema, and returns the parsed big-integer value, throwing an error if validation fails.
This takes no arguments, validates a stored text value against a predefined date schema, and returns the parsed date result, throwing an error if validation fails.

This function takes no arguments, validates a boolean property from an outer object against a big-integer schema, and returns the parsed value. It throws a validation error if the value isn't a valid big integer, which a boolean normally wouldn't be.
This function takes no arguments; it validates an outer value's string property against a boolean schema and returns the parsed boolean, or throws if validation fails.

This function takes no arguments and validates a predefined undefined test value against a boolean schema, returning the parsed boolean or, more likely, throwing a validation error since undefined isn't boolean.
This function takes no arguments; it validates a numeric property from an outer object against a boolean schema and returns the parsed value, throwing an error if validation fails.
This function takes no arguments, validates a "null" property from an outer object against a boolean schema, and returns the resulting boolean, throwing an error if validation fails.
This function takes no arguments, validates a boolean property from an outer object against a date validation schema, and returns the parsed result, throwing an error if validation fails.
This function takes no arguments, validates a numeric property from an outer variable against a date validation schema, and returns the parsed date value, throwing an error if validation fails.
This function takes no arguments, validates a particular stored value against a date validation schema, and returns the parsed date if it is valid, otherwise throwing an error.
This takes no arguments; it validates the numeric field of an outer value against a symbol-validation schema and returns the parsed result, throwing an error if validation fails.
This function takes no arguments, validates a string property from an outer-scope value against a symbol schema, and returns the parsed result, throwing an error if validation fails.
This function takes no arguments, validates a specific property of an external value against a date schema, and returns the parsed date, throwing an error if validation fails.
This takes no arguments, validates an existing value's boolean property against a symbol-validation schema, and returns the parsed result, throwing an error if validation fails.
This function takes no arguments; it validates the date field of an outer object against a symbol-type schema and returns the parsed value, throwing an error if validation fails.
This function takes no arguments, checks that a string property of an outer object is actually undefined, and returns that undefined value, throwing a validation error if it isn't.

This function takes no arguments and validates an undefined test value against a schema expecting a symbol, returning the parsed value; since undefined isn't a symbol, it will typically throw a validation error.

This function takes no inputs and validates a null value against a symbol-type schema. It returns the parsed result if validation succeeds; since null is not a symbol, it typically throws a validation error.
This function takes no arguments, checks that the boolean property of an outside value is undefined, and returns that undefined result, throwing a validation error if it isn't.
This function takes no arguments, checks that a numeric property on an outer object is absent, and returns nothing if so; otherwise it throws a validation error.
This function takes no arguments and validates a particular stored null-related value against a schema that only accepts undefined, returning the parsed result or throwing a validation error.
This function takes no arguments; it validates a string property of an outer object against a schema that accepts only null, returning the parsed value or throwing on failure.
This function takes no arguments; it validates a boolean property from an outer object against a schema that accepts only null, returning the parsed result or throwing on mismatch.
This function takes no arguments; it validates a numeric field from an outer object against a schema expecting null, returning the parsed value if valid and otherwise throwing an error.
This function takes no arguments and validates an undefined value against a schema that accepts only null, returning the parsed result or, more likely, throwing a validation error.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/tests/promise.test.ts: This method accepts no meaningful input, ignoring any error handler passed to it, and simply returns the same object it was called on so calls can keep chaining.
This method takes no arguments and simply returns the object it is called on, allowing calls to be chained without doing any work or changing state.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/tests/record.test.ts#: This function takes no input and validates a hardcoded object with a numeric value against a schema expecting boolean values, so it throws a validation error rather than returning anything.

This function takes no input and validates an object mapping a key to an empty array against a schema expecting boolean values, which presumably throws a validation error rather than returning anything.
This function takes no arguments and tries to validate an object whose single entry holds an empty object instead of a boolean, so validation is expected to throw an error.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/tests/promise.test.ts: This takes no arguments and validates a fake promise-like object, with a callable "then" but a non-callable "catch", against a promise schema, likely throwing a validation error rather than returning anything.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/tests/string.test.ts#: It takes a header object and a payload object, encodes each as URL-safe base64 JSON, and returns a token string joined by dots with a fake placeholder signature.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#processCreat: It takes optional schema configuration options and returns an object with a description and an error-message mapper, either the one supplied or one built from the custom messages given.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#ParseInputLa: This class wraps a value being validated with its parent context, base location, and key, and lazily builds and caches the full location path by appending the key segments.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/tests/tuple.test.ts#c: This function takes no arguments and returns nothing; it validates a sample three-part array (a number, an object with a name, and a list of colors) against a tuple schema, throwing if invalid.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#handleResult: It takes a parsing context and a synchronous parse outcome, returning either a success object with the parsed data or a failure object with a lazily built, cached validation error.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#_getType@172: This method takes a parsing input object and returns a string naming the detected runtime type of the data it contains.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#_getOrReturn: It takes parsing input and an optional existing parsing context, returning that context if given, otherwise building a new one from the input's data, path, parent, detected type, and schema's error map.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#_processInpu: It takes a parsing input and returns a fresh parse status plus a context object holding the data, its detected type, the error map, path, parent, and shared settings.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#ZodType@158: This abstract base class for validation schemas takes unknown input data and validates it, synchronously or asynchronously, returning typed output, a success-or-error result, or thrown errors, with support for custom refinements.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#_parse@170: This abstract method, which each subclass must implement, takes a parsing context with the raw data and returns a result reporting validity and the typed output, possibly asynchronously.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#customMap@13: It takes a validation issue and its context, and returns an error message object, preferring custom messages for enum mismatches, missing values, and wrong types before falling back to the default error.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#_parseAsync@: This method takes parsing input, runs the regular synchronous parse on it, and returns the result wrapped in a resolved promise so callers can treat it asynchronously.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#\"~validate\: It takes an arbitrary input value and validates it against the schema, returning either the parsed value or a list of issues, synchronously when possible and otherwise as a promise.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#_parseSync@2: It takes parsing input, runs the underlying parse, and returns the synchronous result, throwing an error if the parse unexpectedly produced a promise.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#safeParse@22: It takes arbitrary input and optional parsing options, synchronously validates it against a schema, and returns a result object reporting either success with the parsed value or failure with errors, without throwing.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#parse@223: It takes arbitrary input and optional parsing settings, validates it against the schema, and returns the typed validated value, or throws the validation error if checking fails.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#parseAsync@2: It takes unknown input data and optional parsing settings, asynchronously validates it, and returns a promise of the validated output, throwing the validation error if it fails.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#refine@323: It takes a type-guard predicate and an optional error message or error-producing function, and returns a wrapped schema whose validated output is narrowed to the predicate's type.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#getIssueProp: Given a validated value, it returns the error details: a plain message wrapped in an object, the result of calling a message-generating function with that value, or the details object unchanged.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#refine@327: It takes a custom validation function, which may be asynchronous, and an optional error message or error-generating function, and returns a new schema that wraps the original with that extra check.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#refine@331: This takes a validation predicate, which may be asynchronous, plus an optional error message or message-producing callback, and returns a new schema that reports a custom issue when the predicate fails.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#refinement@3: It takes a predicate and either fixed error details or a function producing them, and returns a wrapped schema that reports that error whenever validated output fails the predicate.
Given a type-guard predicate and either fixed issue details or a function producing them, it returns a wrapped schema whose validated output is narrowed to the guarded type.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#setError@346: This function takes no arguments and records a custom validation issue on the current validation context, with details derived from the value being checked, returning nothing meaningful.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#safeParseAsy: It takes arbitrary input data and optional parsing options, validates it asynchronously against the schema, and returns a promise resolving to a success-or-error result instead of throwing.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#refinement@3: This takes a validation predicate plus error details (fixed or computed from the value and context) and returns a wrapped schema that records that error whenever the predicate fails.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#_refinement@: It takes a custom validation callback and returns a new schema that wraps the current one, running that callback as an additional check during parsing.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#optional@444: This method takes no arguments and returns a new schema that wraps the current one, accepting the same values plus undefined, while keeping the original configuration.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#superRefine@: It takes a custom validation callback, which receives the parsed value and a context for reporting issues, and returns a new schema wrapping the original with that validation applied.
It takes a type-guard callback, which receives the parsed value and a context for reporting custom validation issues, and returns a wrapped schema whose output type is narrowed accordingly.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#nullable@447: This method takes no arguments and returns a new schema that wraps the current one, keeping its configuration, and also accepts null as a valid value.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#superRefine@: It takes an asynchronous validation callback that receives the parsed value and a context for reporting custom issues, and returns a wrapped schema applying that validation after parsing.
It takes a custom validation callback that receives the parsed value and a context for reporting issues, and returns a new wrapped schema applying that validation with unchanged types.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#nullish@450: This method takes no arguments and returns a new schema derived from the current one that also accepts both null and undefined, by wrapping it as nullable and then optional.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#promise@456: This method takes no arguments and returns a new schema that validates a promise resolving to a value matching the current schema, carrying over its existing configuration.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#array@453: It takes no arguments and, called on an existing validation schema, returns a new schema that validates lists whose every element must satisfy the original schema.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#and@464: This method takes another validation schema and returns a new combined schema requiring input data to satisfy both the current schema and the provided one, preserving the current schema's configuration.

descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#default@479: It takes a fallback value of the schema's input type (excluding undefined) and returns a wrapped schema that substitutes that value whenever the input is undefined.

descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#catch@502: It takes a callback that receives the validation error and original input and computes a fallback value, returning a wrapped schema that yields that fallback whenever parsing fails.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#pipe@522: This method takes a target validation schema and returns a pipeline that first validates input with the current schema, then passes the result through the target schema.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#describe@514: It takes a text description and returns a new copy of the same kind of object, with identical configuration plus that description attached, leaving the original unchanged.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#readonly@525: This method takes no arguments and returns a new schema that wraps the current one, marking its parsed output as immutable so it cannot be modified.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#isOptional@5: This method takes no arguments and returns a true-or-false value indicating whether the schema accepts an undefined value, meaning the field is optional.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#timeRegex@66: It takes options for timezone offset, local time and fractional-second precision, and returns a regular expression that matches an entire string only if it is a valid time.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#isNullable@5: This method takes no arguments and returns a true or false answer indicating whether the schema accepts an empty value, by trying to validate one and checking whether that succeeds.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#timeRegexSou: It takes an options object with an optional fractional-second precision and returns a regular-expression source string matching 24-hour clock times. Seconds are required when precision is positive, otherwise optional, with fractional digits fixed, arbitrary, or disallowed.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#isValidJWT@6: It takes a token string and an optional expected signing algorithm, and returns true only if the token is well-formed and its decoded header declares an algorithm. descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#datetimeRege: It takes options for fractional-second precision, timezone-offset allowance and local-time allowance, and returns a regular expression matching a full ISO-8601 date-time string under those rules.

descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#isValidIP@68: This function takes an address string and an optional protocol version, and returns true if the string is a valid IPv4 or IPv6 address (restricted to that version if specified).
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#_parse@731: Takes an input value, optionally converts it to text, confirms it is a string, and runs configured checks and transformations, returning the possibly transformed string with any validation issues recorded.

descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#url@1059: It takes an optional custom error message and returns a new string schema that also validates the value as a properly formatted URL.

descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#max@1206: This method takes a maximum length and an optional custom error message, adds a maximum-length validation rule, and returns a new validator that includes that rule.

descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#length@1214: It takes a required exact length and an optional custom error message, adds a validation rule requiring the value to have exactly that length, and returns the updated schema.

descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#toLowerCase@: It takes no arguments and returns a new string validation schema that copies the existing configuration and adds a step converting values to lowercase, leaving the original unchanged.

descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#gt@1467: This method takes a number and an optional custom error message, and returns a new numeric validation schema requiring values to be strictly greater than that number.

descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#int@1502: It takes an optional custom error message and returns a new number schema that also requires the value to be an integer, reporting that message when validation fails.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#_addCheck@14: It takes a numeric validation rule and returns a new number schema with the same settings as the original, plus that rule added to its existing list of rules.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#safe@1561: It takes an optional custom error message and returns a new number schema that only accepts values within JavaScript's safe integer range, inclusive at both ends.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#negative@151: It takes an optional custom error message and returns a new number schema requiring values strictly less than zero, using that message when validation fails.

descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#ZodDate@1875: A date validation schema that takes an input value, optionally converts it to a date, checks it is a valid date within any configured earliest/latest bounds, and returns a copied date or validation errors.

descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#ZodSymbol@20: This schema validator takes an input value and returns it unchanged as a successful result if it is a symbol, otherwise records a type-mismatch error and returns an invalid marker.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#ZodUndefined: This schema validator accepts an input value and returns it as a successful result only if it is undefined; otherwise it records a type-mismatch error and returns an invalid marker.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#min@1948: It takes an earliest allowed date and an optional custom error message, and returns a new date validator that rejects any date before that minimum.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#max@1956: It takes a latest allowed date and an optional custom error message, and returns a new date validation schema that rejects dates after that limit.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#ZodNull@2077: This schema validator takes an input value and returns it as valid only if it is null; otherwise it records a type-mismatch error and returns an invalid result.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#_addCheck@19: It takes a date validation rule and returns a new date schema with the same settings as the original plus that rule appended, leaving the original unchanged.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#ZodAny@2110: This defines a permissive schema type that accepts any input value without validation and returns it unchanged as a successful result, plus a factory for constructing instances from optional parameters.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#_parse@2008: This validation method takes an input value, checks that it is a symbol, and returns the value as a successful result, or records a type-mismatch issue and returns an invalid marker.

descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#_parse@2078: This validation method takes an input value and returns it as a successful result if it is null; otherwise it records a type-mismatch issue and returns an invalid result.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#ZodUnknown@2: This defines a permissive schema type that accepts any input value and returns it unchanged as a successful validation result, with a factory for creating instances from optional settings.

descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#ZodNever@216: This schema type accepts any input value, always records a type-mismatch error noting nothing was expected, and returns an invalid result; its factory builds instances from optional configuration.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#_parse@2191: This validation method accepts parse input and returns a successful result with the data only if the value is undefined; otherwise it records a type-mismatch issue and returns failure.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#ZodArray@223: This defines an array validation schema that takes an input value, checks it is an array meeting optional exact, minimum, or maximum length constraints, and returns a validated result after checking each element.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#_parse@2239: It takes an input value, checks that it is an array meeting any exact, minimum, or maximum length rules, validates each element against the element schema, and returns the merged result.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#max@2326: This method takes a maximum element count and an optional custom error message, and returns a new array validator that requires arrays to contain no more than that many elements.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#nonempty@234: It takes an optional custom error message and returns a copy of the array schema that requires at least one element, typed as a non-empty array.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#min@2319: It takes a minimum element count and an optional error message, and returns a new array validation schema that also requires arrays to contain at least that many items.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#deepPartiali: It takes a validation schema and returns a copy where every object field at every nesting level becomes optional. It recurses through arrays, tuples, optional and nullable wrappers, and leaves other schema types unchanged.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#_parse@2113: This parsing method takes an input context and returns a successful result containing the input's data unchanged, with no validation or transformation, accepting any value.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#length@2333: It takes a required element count and an optional error message, and returns a new array validation schema that only accepts arrays with exactly that many elements.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#extend@2631: It takes a set of additional field schemas and returns a new object schema combining the original fields with the new ones, overriding duplicates, while preserving existing settings.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#_parse@2467: It takes an input value and validates it as an object against a defined schema, handling extra keys by passing them through, rejecting them, stripping them, or checking them against a fallback rule. It returns the validated object result, or a promise of it in asynchronous mode.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#_getCached@2: Taking no arguments, it returns the object schema's field definitions and their key names, computing them on the first call and reusing the stored result afterward.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#ZodObject@24: This schema class validates an input value as an object against a defined set of property validators, handling extra keys by stripping, rejecting, passing through, or validating them, and returns the parsed result.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#setKey@2735: Given a property name and a validation schema, it returns a new object schema that keeps all existing fields and adds or replaces that one property with the given schema.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#strip@2594: It takes no arguments and returns a copy of the object schema configured to silently drop unrecognized keys during parsing, keeping all other settings unchanged.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#strict@2572: It takes an optional custom error message and returns a new copy of the object schema that rejects unrecognized keys. When provided, the message replaces the default text for unrecognized-key errors.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#passthrough@: This method takes no arguments and returns a new copy of the object schema that keeps unrecognized keys in parsed output instead of stripping them or rejecting them.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#deepPartial@: This method takes no arguments and returns a copy of the current schema in which every property, including those nested at any depth, becomes optional.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#omit@2787: It takes a mask object flagging which fields to exclude and returns a new object schema with those fields removed, keeping all other fields and the original settings.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#partial@2812: It takes a selection of field names flagged true and returns a new object schema where those selected fields become optional and all other fields stay unchanged.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#partial@2821: It takes an optional selection of field names and returns a new object schema where those fields (or all fields if none are given) become optional, leaving others unchanged.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#pick@2770: It takes a mask naming selected keys and returns a new object schema with only those fields, keeping the original configuration such as unknown-key handling and catch-all behavior.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#catchall@276: It takes a schema and returns a new copy of the object schema in which any keys not explicitly defined are validated against that given schema.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#partial@2811: Called on an object schema with no arguments, it returns a new object schema in which every property is optional, keeping the original's unknown-key policy and catch-all rule.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#required@284: This method takes no arguments and returns a new object schema identical to the original, except every property is mandatory, while keeping the same unknown-key policy and fallback schema.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#required@285: It takes an optional selection of field names and returns a new object schema where those fields, or all fields if none are given, have every optional wrapper removed, making them mandatory.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#keyof@2874: This method takes no arguments and returns an enumeration schema whose allowed values are exactly the property names defined in the object schema's shape.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#_parse@2945: It takes input data and validates it against several alternative schemas. It returns the first fully valid result, otherwise the first partially valid one with its issues, otherwise an invalid result with an aggregated union error.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#ZodDiscrimin: A validation schema that takes an object, reads a shared tag property to select the matching object schema from a set of alternatives, and returns that schema's parse result or an error.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#ZodUnion@294: It validates an input against several alternative schemas, returning the first fully valid result, otherwise the first partially valid one with its issues, otherwise an invalid status recording every alternative's errors.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#handleResult: This function takes the parse outcomes of each alternative in a union schema and returns the first fully valid result, else the first partially valid one with its issues, else an invalid-union failure.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#required@284: It takes a selection of field names and returns a new object schema where those chosen fields become mandatory, leaving all other fields and settings unchanged.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#_parse@3118: It takes input data, checks that it is an object, and uses a designated key's value to select the matching schema variant. It returns that variant's synchronous or asynchronous validation result, or an invalid marker with a recorded issue if the data isn't an object or no variant matches.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#handleParsed: It takes two parse results for an intersection type, returns an invalid result if either aborted or their values can't be merged, and otherwise returns the merged value with combined status.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#mergeValues@: Takes two values and recursively merges them: objects combine keys, same-length arrays merge element by element, equal dates match. It returns the merged result, or a failure indicator if any part conflicts.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#ZodIntersect: It validates an input against two schemas, synchronously or asynchronously, and returns their merged result, or an invalid result with an issue if the outputs conflict.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#ZodTuple@339: This class validates an input array against a fixed sequence of positional schemas plus an optional trailing schema, returning the parsed elements or validation errors for wrong type or length.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#_parse@3512: It takes an input value, checks that it is an object, validates every key and value against the configured key and value schemas, and returns the merged parse result, either synchronously or asynchronously.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#getDiscrimin: Takes a validation schema and recursively unwraps wrapper types to return the list of exact primitive values it can match, or an empty list if those values can't be determined.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#_parse@3290: It takes an input value, validates it against two schemas (synchronously or asynchronously), and returns their merged result, or an invalid result if either fails or the outputs conflict.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#create@3551: It takes a schema for values plus optional configuration and returns a validation schema for objects whose keys are strings and whose values all match that schema.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#rest@3454: It takes a validation schema for extra trailing elements and returns a new tuple schema, keeping the original settings, that accepts any number of additional items matching that schema.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#ZodRecord@35: This schema class validates an object by checking every key against a key schema and every value against a value schema, returning the parsed dictionary or an invalid-type failure.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#_parse@3397: It takes an input value and checks it is a fixed-length list whose elements match per-position schemas (plus an optional trailing schema), returning the combined validation result, synchronously or asynchronously.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#_parse@3601: It takes an input that should be a map, validates every key and value against their respective schemas, and returns a newly built map of parsed entries with a validity status, synchronously or asynchronously.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#create@3552: <answer>Takes a schema for keys, a schema for values, and optional configuration, and returns a validation schema for dictionary-like objects whose keys and values match those schemas.</answer>
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#ZodMap@3590: This schema class takes an input value, verifies it is a Map, and validates every key and value against their respective schemas. It returns a new parsed Map, synchronously or asynchronously, or an invalid result.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#ZodSet@3684: This schema class validates that an input is a set within optional size bounds, checks each element against an element schema, and returns a new set of parsed elements.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#_parse@3689: It takes an input value, checks that it is a set within the size limits, validates each element against the element schema, and returns a new set or an invalid result.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#min@3753: It takes a minimum element count and an optional error message, and returns a new set schema requiring at least that many elements, leaving the original schema unchanged.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#nonempty@377: This method takes an optional custom error message and returns a new set schema that requires the set to contain at least one element.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#create@3557: It accepts either a key schema, value schema and optional settings, or just a value schema and optional settings. It returns a new record validator, using string keys when no key schema is supplied.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#finalizeSet@: It takes a list of individual validation results and returns an invalid marker if any failed outright; otherwise it returns a set of their values plus an overall status, marked dirty if any were.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#max@3760: It takes a maximum element count and an optional error message, and returns a new set schema that rejects sets with more elements than that limit.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#size@3767: This method takes an exact required count and an optional custom error message, and returns the same validator constrained so the collection must contain exactly that many elements.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#ZodFunction@: This schema takes a function and returns a wrapped version that checks its arguments and return value at every call, synchronously or asynchronously, throwing a validation error on mismatch.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#_parse@3820: Takes an input value, confirms it is a function, and returns a wrapped version that validates its arguments and return value against schemas, synchronously or asynchronously, throwing on mismatch.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#makeArgsIssu: This function takes a function's arguments and the validation error they caused, and returns a validation issue flagging invalid arguments, located at the current path and formatted using the available error-message mappings.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#makeReturnsI: It takes a function's returned value and the validation error it produced. It returns a single validation issue reporting an invalid return type, located at the current path and formatted using whichever error-message maps are available.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#returnType@3: This method takes no arguments and returns the schema describing the expected return value, read from the function schema's internal definition.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#returns@3919: It takes a new return-value schema and returns a new function schema with the same argument definition and settings, but with the return type replaced by the given schema.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#args@3910: It takes any number of schemas describing a function's parameters and returns a new function schema, keeping the existing return type, whose arguments form a tuple of those schemas plus unknown extras.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#parameters@3: This accessor takes no input and returns the schema describing the function's expected arguments, read from the object's internal definition.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#implement@39: It takes a function implementation, wraps it in this function schema so its arguments and return value are validated at runtime, and returns that wrapped function with matching types.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#create@3942: This factory takes no arguments and returns a function schema that accepts any number of arguments of unknown type and produces a value of unknown type.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#create@3945: It takes a schema for a function's argument list, a schema for its return value, and optional configuration, and returns a schema describing a function with that signature.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#create@3943: This factory takes a schema describing a function's argument list, defaulting to no arguments, and returns a function schema with those arguments and an unspecified, unknown return type.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#strictImplem: It takes a function implementation, wraps it through the schema so its arguments and return value are validated at runtime, and returns that validated function with strictly matching types.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#create@3944: This static factory takes a tuple schema for a function's arguments and a schema for its return value, and returns a new function schema combining both.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#create@3950: It takes optional argument and return-type schemas plus configuration options, and returns a new function schema, defaulting to any number of unknown arguments and an unknown return value.

descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#_parse@4005: <answer>It takes an input to validate and checks whether its data exactly equals one expected fixed value, returning a valid result with that data or recording a mismatch issue and returning an invalid marker.</answer>

descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#createZodEnu: It takes a non-empty list of string literals and optional configuration settings, and returns a validation schema that accepts only one of those exact string values.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#_parse@3977: It takes parsing input, lazily obtains the deferred schema it wraps, and returns that schema's validation result for the same data, path and parent context.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#ZodEnum@4077: This validator class accepts input data and returns it unchanged if it's a string from a fixed allowed set, otherwise reporting a type or invalid-option error; it also offers lookup maps and subset-derived validators.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#_parse@4080: It takes an input value and checks that it is a string from a fixed set of allowed options. It returns the value as valid if it matches, or records a type or invalid-option error and returns an invalid result otherwise.

descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#_parse@4177: It takes an input value and checks that it is a string or number matching one of a native enumeration's allowed values, returning it as valid or recording an error and returning invalid.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#ZodNativeEnu: This validator takes an input value and checks that it is a string or number matching one of a native enum's valid values, returning the value if valid or an invalid result with an issue recorded otherwise.

descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#extract@4138: This method takes a non-empty subset of an enum schema's allowed values, plus optional configuration, and returns a new enum schema restricted to those values, inheriting the original's settings.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#_parse@4242: It takes an input value and returns a successful result wrapping a promise that resolves to the inner schema's asynchronously validated value. If the input isn't a promise in synchronous mode, it records a type error and returns an invalid result.

descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#ZodEffects@4: This schema wrapper takes an inner validation schema plus an effect (preprocessing, extra validation check, or value transformation) and returns a parse result reflecting that effect, synchronously or asynchronously.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#_parse@4320: It takes a parse input and applies a schema's attached preprocessing, validation refinement, or transformation around the inner schema's parsing, returning the (possibly asynchronous) result with valid, dirty, or invalid status.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#innerType@43: This method takes no arguments and returns the underlying schema that this wrapper schema wraps, read from its internal definition object.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#executeRefin: It takes a value, runs a validation check on it, and returns a promise of the check's outcome in asynchronous mode. Otherwise it returns the original value, throwing an error if the check unexpectedly turns out asynchronous.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#ZodNullable@: This schema wrapper takes an inner validation schema and accepts null as valid, returning null directly for null input or otherwise delegating validation to the wrapped schema.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#_parse@4488: It takes a parse input and returns a successful empty result if the value is missing, otherwise delegating validation to the wrapped inner schema and returning its result.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#unwrap@4496: This method takes no arguments and returns the inner type stored in the object's definition, exposing the underlying schema that the current wrapper type encloses.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#ZodDefault@4: This schema wrapper takes an input value, substitutes a configured default when the input is undefined, and returns the result of validating it with the wrapped inner schema.

descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#_parse@4567: This method takes parsing input, substitutes a configured default value when the incoming data is undefined, and returns the result of validating that data with the wrapped inner schema.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#_parse@4528: This method takes an input to validate and returns a successful null result if the input is null; otherwise it returns the wrapped schema's validation result.

descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#ZodNaN@4699: This schema validator takes an input value and returns it as valid only if it is the special "not a number" numeric value; otherwise it records a type-mismatch error and returns failure.

descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v3/types.ts#_parse@4875: It takes parsing input, delegates validation to a wrapped inner schema, and returns that result (synchronously or as a promise) with any successfully parsed value shallowly frozen as read-only.

descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v4/core/api.ts#_positive: It takes an optional error message or configuration and returns a validation check requiring a number to be strictly greater than zero.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v4/core/api.ts#_nonnegat: This function takes an optional error message or configuration options and returns a validation check requiring a numeric value to be greater than or equal to zero.
descriptions.zod-3.25.76/src/v4/core/api.ts#_nonposit: This function takes an optional error message or configuration options and returns a validation check requiring a number to be less than or equal to zero.
